bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 12117) lists Umm Tariq, freedwoman (mawla) of Sa'd bin 'Ubada al-Ansari, chief of the Khazraj. Ibn Abi al-Dunya also included it in his work on illness and expiations.

bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 11430) lists Duba'a bint 'Amir bin Qurt bin Salama bin Qushayr of 'Amir bin Sa'sa'a. Citing Abu Nu'aym, it describes her as one of the women who accepted Islam with the Prophet in Mecca. bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba has two entries named Abd Allah ibn Badr on this page. bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 5559) says al-Bardiji listed him in al-Asma' al-Mufrada in the first tier; some spell the name with ghayn, and some say he was not a Companion. Sa'id ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz said he used to live at Bayt Lahya, was one of the companions of Mu'adh ibn Jabal, and his father is unknown. Ibn Abi Khaythama also recorded him.

full_name_ar: عصام بن عامر الكلبي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 5561) cites Abu Sa'id al-Naysaburi's Sharaf al-Mustafa: 'Isam was custodian of an idol called 'Umra, and heard a voice from inside it announcing that Islam had come and the idols had gone. He then travelled with 'Amr ibn Jabala ibn Wa'ila al-Kalbi to the Prophet, who invited them to Islam, and they accepted.

full_name_ar: عصمة بن المثنى ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 5569, marked as Ibn Hajar's addition) cites al-Tabari that 'Umar sent him as commander of reinforcements to al-Muthanna ibn Haritha after the killing of Abu 'Ubayd. The entry also mentions his part in Nu'aym ibn Muqarrin's campaign for the conquest of Jurjan.

bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 5578) gives him as of Banu Sahm of Quraysh and cites al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar: his brother al-'As ibn Qays was killed as an unbeliever at Badr. The line of Qays ibn 'Abd Qays died out except through 'Ata', whose descendants lived in Egypt.

full_name_ar: عطاء الشيبي قيل ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 5580) says he was said to be the son of 'Abd Allah, or of al-Nadr ibn al-Harith. He lived in Kufa and is reported to have seen the Prophet praying in sandals, via Fitr ibn Khalifa from a shaykh named 'Ata'. The transmitter Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Asadi is described as very weak, and Abu 'Umar (Ibn 'Abd al-Barr) and Ibn Mandah question his companionship.

bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 5581) says al-Hasan ibn Sufyan transmitted his hadith via Ayyub ibn Waqid from his son 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ata'. The hadith is a saying of the Prophet about the muezzin between the adhan and the iqama.

full_name_ar: عطية بن عمرو الغفاري ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 5591) says Ibn Shahin listed him, quoting Ahmad ibn Sayyar that al-Hakam ibn 'Amr had a brother called 'Atiyya ibn 'Amr who was a Companion. 'Ali ibn Mujahid also said that 'Atiyya ibn 'Amr and his brother al-Hakam ibn 'Amr were both Companions.

full_name_ar: عقبة بن رافع الأنصاري ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 5613) says he is mentioned in Sahih Muslim, where Anas reports the Prophet saw in a dream that he was in the house of 'Uqba ibn Rafi'. Ibn Mandah mis-copied this under 'Uqba ibn Nafi' and Abu Nu'aym corrected him. Abu Ya'la and al-Hasan ibn Sufyan report via Mahmud ibn Labid from 'Uqba ibn Rafi' a hadith attributed to the Prophet: 'When Allah loves a servant, He shields him from the world.'

full_name_ar: عقبة بن مالك الجهني ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 5628) says Ibn Qani' listed him, with a hadith via Shahr ibn Hawshab about arrogance barring entry to Paradise. A report by Ibn Shahin about his sister's vow is, per Abu Musa, really from 'Uqba ibn 'Amir al-Juhani and 'ibn Malik' there is a copyist's error. Al-Tabarani's al-Awsat has another hadith from him about seeking Laylat al-Qadr in the odd nights of the last ten of Ramadan.

full_name_ar: علباء السلمي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 5672) quotes Abu Hatim that he was a Companion. Al-Bukhari cites via Ahmad ibn Hanbal and 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far from his father from 'Ilba' that he heard the Prophet say the Hour will come only upon the dregs of mankind. The hadith is also recorded by al-Hakim, al-Baghawi and Ibn Abi 'Asim, and Ibn 'Adi notes 'Ali ibn Thabit alone narrated it from 'Abd al-Hamid.
research_evidence: ٥٦٧٢- علباء السلمي قال أبو حاتم: له صحبة.

full_name_ar: عمرو بن سعيد الهذلي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 5863, 'Amr ibn Sa'id al-Hudhali) says Abu Nu'aym listed him among the Companions, via Hatim ibn Isma'il from 'Abd Allah ibn Yazid al-Hudhali from his son Sa'id ibn 'Amr. He was an old man who lived through both the Jahiliyya and Islam. The entry includes an account about the idol Suwa' and his acceptance of Islam at the conquest of Mecca.

full_name_ar: عمرو بن شبيل الثقفي ( رضي الله عنه
generation: Mukhadram / Successor — lived in the Prophet's era but is not recorded as having met him
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 5882) says he was of Banu 'Attab ibn Malik of Thaqif, and that al-Marzubani called him a mukhadram (lived in both the Jahiliyya and Islam) and quoted his poetry. Ibn Hajar adds that Usd al-Ghaba says he witnessed the Pledge of Ridwan under the tree and was married to Habiba bint Mut'im ibn 'Adi; Ibn al-Dabbagh added him as a supplement.
